---
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Paper template. Copy to papers/<slug>/index.qmd and create three sibling
# folders alongside it:
#
#   latex/     the original .tex source, .bib file, and any figures
#   pdf/       the compiled PDF
#   sessions/  dumps of prompt/agent research sessions behind the write-up,
#              named YYYY-MM-DD-<prompt-name>.md. Excluded from the rendered
#              site; kept for provenance only.
#
# A paper carries a status badge graded on the same scale as a statement
# leaf, but none of a leaf's taxonomy: no id, no problem hub, no areas, no
# relations, no lean block. Add the new paper by hand to the "## Papers"
# list in papers/archive/index.qmd -- that list is written, not generated.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
title: "Title of the paper"

# Optional, for a subheading the title itself should not carry.
subtitle: ""

# Include the AI as a named collaborator where it was one, e.g.
# "Jane Doe, with Claude (Anthropic)".
author: ""

date: 2026-01-01

# Free-form topic tags, display only. Unlike a statement leaf's `areas`,
# these are not drawn from a fixed vocabulary.
categories: []

# Starts empty. Once a Programme Committee member reviews this paper, add
# their name here; the list accumulates across reviews rather than being
# overwritten. See papers/programme-committee/index.qmd.
reviewers: []

# The same six fields a statement leaf carries, unchanged in meaning or
# grading, for now graded at the level of the whole paper. See
# scripts/status_badge.py and /open-problems/status-legend/.
status:
  statement_informal: ai
  statement_formal: open
  statement_match: open
  proof_informal: open
  proof_review: ai
  proof_formal: open

# One required sentence saying where the paper's central result actually
# stands. It is rendered next to the badge, so it should be readable
# without opening the paper.
status_summary: "One-sentence summary of where this paper's central result actually stands."

status_updated: 2026-01-01

# Bumped by scripts/status_badge.py when statement_sha changes.
revision: 1

# Hash of the '## Statement' tab content below, script-maintained by
# scripts/status_badge.py. Leave this EMPTY for a new paper -- the script
# fills it in silently on first run. A non-empty value that later stops
# matching is what triggers the loud warning (forces statement_match back
# to open, bumps revision); an empty value never does.
statement_sha: ""

# Generated by scripts/status_badge.py. Never hand-edit.
status_badge: "<generated, never hand-edited>"
---

<!-- status:start -->
<!-- regenerated by scripts/status_badge.py -- do not hand-edit between these markers -->
<!-- status:end -->

cryptography problem of wider interest that is not itself posted as a
conjecture on this site. This section (from this heading to the next) is
exactly what `statement_sha` hashes.

## Proof

Describe the paper's proof or argument here, or note that this is a
survey/exposition with no new proof of its own.
